pr.title: Draw a draft's review label in italic, as its number is
pr.head: 432f33e5b11f7283e96b51069f0c6a165f547cc9

summary: Projector's panel in Claude Code lists the session's pull requests, one row each. A row starts with the pull request's number and then a state word: reviewing in orange or clean in green when the pull request carries that review label, and otherwise draft or ready. A draft is a pull request whose author is still working on it.

Before this change, a draft's number and the word draft were italic, but a review label on a draft was drawn upright. A held draft, which keeps its clean label while its author builds a change, therefore showed the same upright green clean as a ready pull request, and only the number said it was a draft.

Now the row draws its state word in italic whenever the pull request is a draft, whatever the word is. The color still comes from the label, so a draft shows an italic green clean, an italic orange reviewing, or an italic draft. A ready pull request's word stays upright.

groups.title: The row's state word follows the draft state
groups.kicker: Italic now comes from the pull request, not from which word the row shows
intro: rowState picks a row's state word and its color. It used to return an italic flag too, set only for the word draft, so a review label never came out italic. The change drops that flag, and the row's renderer sets the word's italic from pr.isDraft, the same field it already used for the number.

The panel test reads each row's word, color, and italic state for five pull requests. The held draft's expectation changes from upright to italic green clean; the other four rows keep their expectations, so the test still says a ready pull request's word is upright.

checks.text: The test catches the change both ways. In a scratch worktree, removing italic from the word, and setting it on every row, each turned the row test red while the other 228 tests passed.
A loading row stays upright. It draws no state word, and loadingOf builds it with isDraft: false, so its number is upright too.

files.note: Drops rowState's italic flag and draws the state word in italic from pr.isDraft.

checks.text: The docstring says draft is in the default color and ready in the theme's light blue. That matches rowState, which returns draft with no color and ready with suggestion. A second commit made this wording change after the first review suggested it.
rowState has no other caller, so removing isItalic from its return type leaves nothing reading it. hooks/typecheck.sh passed.

files.note: Expects the held draft's clean in italic green, and renames the test to say the word is italic too.

groups.title: The panel's documentation
groups.kicker: docs/plugins.md describes the italic state word
intro: The panel section of docs/plugins.md now says that a draft's number and state are both italic, that draft is in the default text color, and that a held draft reads as an italic number beside an italic green clean.

files.note: Describes the row's italic state word on a draft.
